rows.title: Find an address by postcode before the address form, in the address book and in the consignee, importer and place of destination sections
rows.detail: Adding an address in the address book, or from the consignee, importer or place of destination section of a notification, starts with a find-address step: the trader enters a UK postcode, picks the address from those found there, and lands on the address form filled in from it, or chooses to enter the address by hand. The addresses come from the INS backend's address lookup. Address search is parked as concept work and waits on the INS backend's address lookup becoming a real feature, so this row waits; until then every add-address page offers manual entry only.
acceptanceCriteria: Adding an address from the consignee, importer or place of destination section, or in the address book, opens a find-address page first; adding one from the place of origin, consignor, county parish holding or permanent address section opens the address form with no find-address page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-010; ruling:paul-2026-11-05 ruling-paul-2026-11-05-p1-030; ruling:ian-2026-11-16 ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-043)
The address book's find-address page is headed 'Add an address'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-005)

On the address book's find-address and select pages the cancel link reads 'Cancel and return to address book' and opens the address book list, and the find-address page's Back link opens the address book's add page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-006, -p17-008)

A section's find-address page is headed 'Add an address for a consignee', 'Add an address for an importer' or 'Add an address for a place of destination', by section. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-013; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p7-046; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-070)

On a section's find-address and select pages the cancel link reads 'Cancel and return to hub' and opens the notification's overview, and the find-address page's Back link opens that section's page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-014, -p17-016; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p7-047; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-071)

The find-address page has one text field labelled 'Enter a UK postcode' with the hint 'For example, AB12 3CD', ten characters wide, with postal-code autocomplete and spellcheck turned off, and a 'Find address' button. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-020; repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p8-008, repo-insfrontend-p8-009)

Below the form on the find-address page and on the select page, whether or not addresses were found, an 'Enter address manually' link comes first and the cancel link second, and 'Enter address manually' opens the same address form empty, to fill in by hand. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-010)

The find-address and select pages' browser title is the page heading, with 'Error: ' in front when the page shows an error, and both pages show the Alpha phase banner with its 'give your feedback by email' link. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-005; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p7-046)

Finding an address with no postcode shows 'Enter a postcode', and with a postcode that is not a full UK postcode, such as 'M1', shows 'Enter a full UK postcode, like BB4 4AA'; each error shows in a 'There is a problem' summary linked to the postcode field and beside the field, which keeps what the trader typed. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-025; repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p8-011; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-088)

A postcode typed in lower case or without its space, such as 'bb44aa', or 'GIR 0AA', is accepted as a full UK postcode, and the find-address step shows it in upper case as its outward code, a space and its inward code, such as 'BB4 4AA', on the select page's postcode line, in its 'No addresses found for' heading, in each address option and in the postcode field of the address form it fills. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-025, -p17-040; repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p8-011)

Submitting a full postcode opens the select page for that postcode, which searches the postcode it shows; opening or submitting the select page without a full postcode opens the find-address page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-033)

With addresses found, the select page is headed and titled 'Select an address' and shows 'Postcode' with the postcode in bold beneath it and a 'Change postcode' link, then a plain full-width select labelled 'Select an address' whose first option has no value and reads '1 address found' or '<N> addresses found', each address one line ending with its postcode shown once, such as 'UNIT 1, YORK AVENUE, HASLINGDEN, BB4 4AA', and a 'Continue' button. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-033, -p17-038, -p17-039, -p17-040; repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p8-023, repo-insfrontend-p8-024; repo:stub repo-stub-p1-010)

With no addresses found, the select page is titled 'No addresses found' and headed 'No addresses found for <postcode>', shows 'Postcode' with the postcode and a 'Change postcode' link, then 'Enter address manually' and the cancel link, and no address list and no Continue button. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-033; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p7-046)

The select page's Back link and its 'Change postcode' link open the find-address page with the postcode searched filled in. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-033; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-090)

Continuing on the select page with no address chosen, or with one not among those found, shows 'Select an address' in a 'There is a problem' summary linked to the select and beside the select; shown again after an error, the select keeps the address the trader picked. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-038, -p17-039)

Continuing with a chosen address opens the address form the find-address page was reached from, the address book's add form or the section's add-address page, with address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode filled from the address's sub-building, building name, number, street and locality, the country set to United Kingdom, name or organisation and county left blank, and every field editable. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p17-049; repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p8-049 to -p8-053; repo:stub repo-stub-p1-014, repo-stub-p1-015; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p7-065)

On the local and CI docker stacks the addresses listed for a postcode are those the stub's address lookup simulator returns to a postcode search through the INS backend's address lookup, such as the three London addresses for 'SW1A 1AA' and none for 'ZZ1 1ZZ'; in CDP they are those the INS backend's address lookup returns. (repo:insfrontend repo-insfrontend-p8-060, repo-insfrontend-p8-061; repo:stub repo-stub-p1-001, repo-stub-p1-002, repo-stub-p1-003, repo-stub-p1-010; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-066)
openQuestions: Blocked: address search is parked as concept work that the deadline does not need (ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2), and it waits on the INS backend's address lookup becoming a real feature; today only a spike exists, gated to dev and local on a page nothing links to (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 178). Who: Sam must plan address search again, and the INS backend's owners must make the lookup real; the address search area is then re-distilled and this row rewritten to it.
rows.notes: Drafter, address-lookup area, re-distil 27 November. One slice: the find-address and select pages, shared by the address book's add journey and the three receiving consignment address sections, combined because both mount the same two pages, validation, postcode formatting and lookup call; splitting by entry point would repeat that set-up. Every requirement is blocked by the same parking (c-507), so they sit together, apart from rows that can build now. The section choice follows the address book's UK-only rule for consignee, importer and place of destination (c-506); the pages search by postcode only, not free text (c-509); the addresses come from the INS backend's lookup, not the prototype's fixture (c-508). Kept here rather than handed to the split-off address-book, consignment-parties and transporters branches: none of them can build it until the parking lifts, and the new pages live in their own new feature folders. The existing lookup clients, the add form, the party picker, the stub simulator and the INS backend lookup are listed under shared, since split-off branches own them; this row reads them, and any change it needs there goes through those owners when the row is re-distilled. The party-address area's postcode-step requirements share the existing row; the combiner joins them. Plants takes the same step for any of these sections it has, when this row is re-distilled.
